To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spontaneous excitation rate of an atom interacting with a thermal bath at a finite temperature is different from the spontaneous excitation rates of the same atom interacting with a bath at the Fullin–Davies temperature and with the Minkowski bath.

(i) the spontaneous excitation rate of a uniformly accelerated atom interacting with the Minkowski scalar vacuum is not invariant under the boost transformation and (ii) it depends on the temperature of the bath to which the coaccelerating observer is in contact.

the spontaneous excitation rate of a uniformly accelerated atom is the same in the coacceleration frame as in the inertial one only if the coaccelerating observer assumes a thermal bath at a temperature T FDU, and that the Fulling– Daves–Unruh effect is not a thermalization phenomenon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a quantum field theory in a noninertial reference frame.
the following question: What is the thermal bath that an inertial observer should consider when analyzing the spontaneous excitation rate of an atom uniformly accelerated in the Minkowskian vacuum?
the study of the Fulling–Davis–Unruh effect in the context of a two-level atom interacting in a thermal bath.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spontaneous excitation rate of the accelerated two-level atom in the inertial Minkowski vacuum is not a universal constant and is dependent on the choice of the reference frame.
the Fulling–Davis–Unruh effect is not a physical effect, but a mathematical artifact of the use of an improper reference frame.

a uniformly accelerated observer, in a thermal bath at T > T FDU, would not see any spontaneous excitation of the atom, whereas the same observer, in a bath at T < T FDU, or in the Minkowskian vacuum, would see a spontaneous excitation of its own atom.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Minkowski and Rindler observers agree on a thermal bath at T FDU for the uniformly accelerated two-level atomic system.
in the coacceleration frame the thermal effect of the Minkowski bath at temperature T is equivalent to the thermal effect of a bath at temperature T FDU.
the spontaneous excitation rate of the uniformly accelerated atom can only be recovered by the coaccelerating observer assuming the Fulling–Davis–Unruh thermal bath at the temperature T FDU.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fulling– Davies–Unruh effect is a genuine quantum effect that cannot be explained in a classical way.

the spontaneous excitation rate of a uniformly accelerated atom interacting with an accelerated quantum field is not a property of the atom itself, but of the interaction between the atom and the quantum field in a specific reference frame.

the thermal character of the Fulling– Davies–Unruh effect can also be understood from the point of the coaccelerating observer as a spontaneous excitation rate of a uniformly accelerated atom in a thermal bath.
